name: Schloss Fernsteinsee & Bergsee
kurzbeschreibung: The fairy-tale waterside castle by the idyllic Fernsteinsee blends history, gastronomy, and a dreamy lake-and-landscape setting.
preis: Kostenlos frei zugänglich (Bootsverleih ca. 10–15 € pro Stunde; Parkplatz ca. 5 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

Schloss Fernsteinsee and its shimmering emerald mountain lake constitute a fairytale cultural and natural landmark nestled at the base of the storied Fern Pass near Nassereith in the Tyrolean Außerfern. Sheltered by fragrant pine forests and the sheer limestone ramparts of the Mieming Range, this historic estate rests at 936 meters elevation. The stronghold's origins date back to the 12th century, functioning as a vital defensive garrison and toll house along the Roman Via Claudia Augusta. Rising from a densely wooded island in the center of the lake stands the romantic Sigmundsburg Castle ruins, constructed around 1460 by Duke Sigmund the Wealthy for his Scottish consort, Eleanor. In the 19th century, King Ludwig II of Bavaria fell under the hypnotic spell of the lake, establishing personal royal suites within the castle. Fed by pristine subterranean springs, the crystal-clear water achieves visibility exceeding 20 meters, making it a world-renowned pilgrimage site for scuba divers and wilderness purists.

Route & Requirements

Exploring Lake Fernsteinsee and the heritage castle estate delivers a delightfully gentle lakeside ramble suited for all generations. A well-graded, peaceful woodland circuit encircles the lake in roughly 45 to 60 minutes (distance approx. 2.5 km, easy grade T1, accessible for rugged all-terrain strollers). Shoreline clearings reveal picture-postcard vistas of the island ruins and castle towers reflecting across glassy emerald waters. In summer, traditional pedal and row boats are available for hire at the boathouse, allowing silent exploration around the island sanctuary. For technical scuba divers, Fernsteinsee is internationally celebrated for submerged timber forests and otherworldly underwater topography (diving reserved for hotel guests with permits). The castle operates as a boutique heritage hotel whose panoramic restaurant and lakeside veranda are open to day visitors. Casual walking shoes suffice. Leashed dogs are permitted on all shoreline paths.

Visit & Arrival

Rail transit arrives via Imst-Pitztal or Telfs-Pfaffenhofen railway stations, connecting to regional VVT bus line 150/160 along the Fernpass route, which stops directly at "Nassereith Fernsteinsee" beside the estate gates. Motorists travel via the Fernpass highway B179 connecting Reutte and Nassereith. Generous parking is provided on-site for restaurant and walking patrons. The lakeside trails remain open year-round with free public access.

Tips

Rent a wooden rowboat from the hotel pier to glide silently across emerald-green water circling the romantic Sigmundsburg island ruins. Afterward, take a seat on the castle restaurant terrace to savor a generous slice of artisanal homemade Fernsteinsee cake with fresh coffee.
